Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase in this decider! The Aussies are in a huddle just outside the boundary ropes where Josh Inglis is giving a last-minute pep talk. Now, they spread out to take their respective field positions. Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique are the two openers for Pakistan. Spencer Johnson to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

There is not much to say about Australia's batting performance. They struggled once again to handle the express pace and swing from the Pakistan bowlers and no one really stepped up in this game in the absence of the big players. Matthew Short looked good at the top but it was Sean Abbott who top-scored with a handy 30 off 41. The injury to Cooper Connolly didn't help but there were six single-digit scores which says a lot about this effort. A return to the ODI side after almost a year did not work out for Marcus Stoinis while Glenn Maxwell became a victim of Haris Rauf for the third time in the series. It is a sorry-looking scorecard, and now the bowlers will have to do something really extraordinary to stop Pakistan from sealing a memorable series win. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

A world-class display of fast bowling from Pakistan! This is exactly what they used to do to teams in the past and it is great to see them performing well at the top level. The Men in Green have put them in a solid position to wrap up a memorable series win over the Aussies on Australian soil and create history. The hosts have never won an ODI at the Optus Stadium and once again, they are starring down the barrel of another defeat.

Naseem Shah set the tone early by getting rid of Jake Fraser-McGurk in the fourth over. After that, they never really looked back and continued to pile the pressure on the Aussies. The pace battery of Pakistan exploited the conditions brilliantly and gave nothing away. Shaheen Afridi was at his absolute best and ended up with three wickets while Shah also picked up three. Haris Rauf continued his good form and got a couple taking his tally to 10 in this series while Mohammad Hasnain chipped in with one. Mohammad Rizwan used only these four bowlers, and they did the job for their skipper bowling Australia for just 140 inside 32 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: In all readiness for the action to begin! The two umpires stride out to the centre! The Pakistan team takes to the field, spreading out with purpose and intensity while Mohammad Rizwan has a big smile on his face. Australian openers, Matthew Short and Jake Fraser-McGurk walk confidently to the crease, ready to face the challenge ahead. At the top of his mark is Shaheen Afridi ready to start the proceedings. Here we go!
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Abdullah Shafique, Saim Ayub, Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan(C/WK), Kamran Ghulam, Salman Agha, Irfan Khan, Shaheen Afridi, Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf, Mohammad Hasnain.
Australia (Playing XI) - Matthew Short, Jake Fraser-McGurk, Aaron Hardie, Josh Inglis (C/WK), Cooper Connolly, Marcus Stoinis, Glenn Maxwell, Sean Abbott, Adam Zampa, Spencer Johnson, Lance Morris.
TOSS - Pakistan have won the coin flip and they have decided to bowl first!

Pakistan, meanwhile, comes into the decider brimming with confidence and momentum. Haris Rauf, clearly benefiting from his Big Bash League experience, has been phenomenal with 8 wickets in 2 games, including a brilliant five-for last match. Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah have also thrived on these pace-friendly wickets. Their openers, Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique, found form just in time, though Babar Azam's performance remains a concern. Skipper Rizwan has been steady in the middle order, adding consistency. Newcomers Kamran Ghulam and Irfan Khan will be eager to make their mark and push Pakistan toward a memorable series win. Will the Men in Green make history, or can Australia mount a comeback? Stay tuned - Toss and team news are coming right up.

With Cummins absent, Josh Inglis steps up to lead the side. Matthew Short and Jake Fraser-McGurk have a prime opportunity to stake their claim for a future opening spot. The bowling lineup may look a bit different, but with three top-notch all-rounders like Stoinis, Maxwell, and Hardie, the team gains a solid balance. The young players will be eager to make an impact, and familiar home conditions should boost their confidence heading into this decider.

Australia grabbed the lead with a hard-fought victory, thanks to skipper Pat Cummins’ clutch performance with the bat. But the visitors struck back with commanding dominance in the second game. Truthfully, Australia’s batting has looked shaky in both matches, and now, with the 'big five' – Smith, Marnus, Starc, Hazlewood, and Cummins – rested ahead of the upcoming Test series, it’ll be intriguing to see how they rise to the challenge in this series decider.

Hello and a warm welcome, everyone! The Australian summer has kicked off with a thrilling start. The three-match ODI series against Pakistan is perfectly poised at 1-1, setting the stage for an exciting decider at the stunning Optus Stadium in Burswood. We’ve been treated to some fantastic cricket across the first two games, and with the stakes higher than ever, more entertainment is certainly on the cards.
... MATCH DAY ...

The caravan has moved to Perth for the third and final ODI between Australia and Pakistan, with the series perfectly poised at 1-1. The Perth Stadium will serve as the stage for this deciding clash, and both teams will be eager to secure the series victory. In the second ODI in Adelaide, Pakistan’s pace attack was relentless, where they bowled out Australia for a modest 163 before comfortably chasing it down with just one wicket lost in 26.3 overs. Australia will be looking for a swift turnaround after the heavy defeat in Adelaide, but they will have to do so without some of their most seasoned players. Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Steven Smith, and Marnus Labuschagne have been rested to ensure they are fresh for the upcoming Test series against India. Josh Inglis will lead a relatively inexperienced squad, particularly in the bowling department, with opportunities likely for Lance Morris, Xavier Bartlett, and Spencer Johnson to step up and fill the void left by the rested pace trio. Marcus Stoinis, who has yet to feature in the series, is expected to slot in and lend some much-needed experience in both batting and bowling. For Pakistan, Haris Rauf spearheaded their bowling effort with a superb five-wicket haul, building on his form from Melbourne, while the rest of the pace attack provided excellent support to stifle Australia’s batting. The visitors head into the Perth decider with momentum firmly in their grasp, following a clinical display in Adelaide. Historically, they have been a team that has become difficult to stop once they have gathered momentum, whether in bilateral series or ICC tournaments. A win here would be momentous for Pakistan, who haven’t clinched an ODI series in Australia since 2002. Since then, they have faced heavy defeats, with scorelines of 5-0 and 4-1 in favour of the hosts. With Australia missing five key players in this match, Pakistan have a golden opportunity to rewrite history in Perth. Can they make it happen and turn the series in their favour? We shall find out soon enough.
